data.body: FULL-SUITE PRE-FLIGHT CAUGHT A REAL INTEGRATION BREAK that my held-out oracle did not: tests/unit/test_project_portability_criterion.py::test_production_fan_in failed (7664 passed, 1 failed, make test exit 2). Two causes, both from story B adding a SECOND project criterion: (1) that test copies the shipped .rebar/criteria_routing.json into a sandbox but copied only ONE rubric, so the sandbox activated a criterion whose prompt was absent -> CriteriaError 'cannot load criterion prompt'; fixed by copying every committed .rebar/prompts/*.md, which is future-proof for further criteria. (2) it asserted batch_resolution['project'] == [project.portability] - equality, so a second activated criterion breaks it; loosened to membership, since the test's point is that portability fans in, not that it is alone. Both fixes are minimal and belong to story B (which introduced the second criterion), so they were amended into B's commit (a7eca139c). Note for the record: this is exactly the value of running the project's own full gate rather than only the leaf's oracle - a held-out oracle scoped to the new criterion could not have seen a sibling test's hardcoded assumption. Story A committed on top (df088d675) after fixing an E501 in my own test file. Final full-suite pre-flight running over the C-and-D-landed main with both A and B applied.
